geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the primary mass into a more explicit split-wing composition so the void becomes a governing spatial figure.
Widen the inter-wing gap to strengthen public void clarity and prevent the mass from reading as a single box.
Keep a ground-level connector so the split remains a coherent neighborhood building rather than two detached fragments.
Strengthen the threshold band at grade to support public entry and active frontage.
Make the ground connector thick enough to read as a usable public threshold.
Lower the upper mass slightly so the section feels calmer and less top-heavy for neighborhood living.

graph_edits.rationale: The primary bar needs to become a clearer single spatial rule with an explicit carved court/threshold rather than reading as a generic rectangular extrusion.
Keep the dominant long-axis organization but make it structurally clearer as the main gesture.
Slightly reduce bulk so the split and void read more clearly and the form stops collapsing into a box.
Add a real public court/opening linked to the access edge so the ground condition becomes legible and programmatic.
Create a meaningful, occupiable void rather than a thin subtraction.
Align the public void to the program's site-access side so the frontage reads as an entry threshold.

rationale: The candidate reads as a split-block mass, but the split is not convincingly legible across all views: in some views the two lobes collide or compress into a near-box, and the central void never becomes a clear public court or entry seam. The verified road frontage/access edge is not answered strongly; the mass remains semantically sealed relative to the access side instead of opening a public threshold. For neighborhood living, the massing needs an active ground relation, a more coherent hierarchy, and a clearer section/public-void logic. It is not a hard typology mismatch, but it is presently too generic and too closed to pass program fit.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more openly public and courtyard-centered than this candidate; candidate should not copy the transparency, only the void/public-threshold logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low, elongated mass with a strong internal void and an active public edge; use the court/atrium as the legible ground response rather than filling the whole envelope.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Single-story restaurant language is not a direct typology match for this 5-floor neighborhood program; avoid turning the project into a shallow pavilion.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact low-rise pavilion with a clear setback/canopy at entry and a simple service-like vertical accent; good for calibrating street threshold and ground-level legibility.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual high-rise residential reference; the candidate is too boxy and too low on public/sectional articulation to inherit this logic directly.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/stepped massing can work when it produces inhabitable roof/section and courtyard continuity.

warnings: Parcel containment cannot be fully verified from the provided image crop; if the green boundary is authoritative, the candidate appears to fit broadly but still needs a clearer response to it.
The blue access edge is not met with a sufficiently legible public seam or court.
Visible view coherence is weak: the mass changes character too much between axonometric and orthographic views.
